transcript.text: Zanussi dishwasher keeps tripping the electrics, not every time though. Usually about 15 mins in. Model ZDT21006FA

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. A dishwasher tripping the mains RCD is a safety hazard and indicates an electrical fault, likely a component shorting to earth. The most common cause for a trip occurring specifically around 15 minutes into a cycle is a failing heater element; as it heats up, insulation breakdown can allow current to leak to the chassis. Other possibilities include a wet circulation pump or a faulty mains filter. Because this involves live electrical parts and water, you must not use the appliance until an engineer has inspected it. To help identify the likely culprit before they arrive: does the trip happen exactly when the water starts to heat (usually around 15 minutes in), or does it happen at a different point, like immediately on start-up or during draining?

It's usually about 10-20 mins in on the 65C programme, so probably when it's heating. The quick cold rinse has never tripped it. The trip takes out a whole bank of circuits including the fridge, so I've left it unplugged for now.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
That timing suggests it is probably a component shorting to earth as it gets hot or wet—most likely the heater element itself. Because this involves live electrical parts and water, you must not use the appliance until a qualified engineer has inspected and repaired it. They will need to isolate the machine, test the insulation resistance of the heater and other components, and replace the faulty part (usually the heater assembly). Please keep it unplugged and arrange for an engineer visit.
